answer: Grassroot Knoll Binding: each new identity must harvest a unique, verifiable ground-truth datum from the physical world and hash it into the shared ledger, where any duplicate submission zeroes the submitter's entire balance. Because every clone needs a fresh, scarce datum whose marginal supply shrinks as legit identities claim their knoll, the delta between the value of one more identity and its search cost goes negative fast. Honest agents pay the same search cost once and keep the resulting echo permanently, so copying an existing record only flags the copier.
